svg.title: RIEMANN · MAP F1 — What the stages pass to each other: the 24 definitions of the blueprint, how they are built from one another, and which chapters use each
svg.desc: Every other poster follows the theorems. This one follows the definitions: the objects one chapter of the proof makes and another consumes. Each card is one of the blueprint's definitions, with the Lean declaration it stands for, the definition in words, and the chapter that makes it in its pill. Read the grid from the foot up: a definition stands above the definitions stated in terms of it, and an arrow from A to B says that B is defined using A. The table at the foot is the flow between stages: for each definition, how many statements of each chapter use it, with the chapter that makes it marked. The outline's own section on the interfaces names three definitions as what the arithmetic stages pass to the analytic ones; those three are used by 35 statements in 7 chapters. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted.

the flow between stages: for each definition, how many statements of each chapter use it, with the chapter that makes it marked. The outline's own section on the interfaces names three definitions as what the arithmetic stages pass to the analytic ones; those three are used by 35 statements in 7 chapters. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted.
A → B: definition B is stated in terms of A (the arrow takes A's colour)

Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands. Main.lean marks the theorems the

The line in italics gives the statement's id and how many paragraphs the blueprint spends on its statement and its proof. The text itself is not quoted: it is the blueprint's authors', and the blueprint link in the
footer has it. The Lean signature is not quoted either, for the same reason; the footer gives the declaration's name, file and line in the mirror.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges, in full. An arrow from A to B: the proof of B uses A, and the arrow takes A's colour.
Used in counts the statements of each chapter that use the definition, in their statement or their proof; it is the row of the table at the foot. The pill names the chapter that makes the definition.
